text:
incident-bot: Pager opened: high inference tail latency detected for hosted region us-west-2. P50 ok, P95/P99 elevated. Alert: queue_depth > 1200, gpu_pool_util > 95% for 4m. Assigning @maya (primary on-call) and paging rotation. https://grafana.redwood.local/d/latency 

maya: picking up. reading dashboards now. seeing a big jump in queued requests around 17:04 UTC.

sam: noted increased external traffic from a partner customer at ~17:02, could be traffic spike.

maya: symptoms: slow streaming responses, clients timing out. customers reporting errors 504. Can someone grep logs for HPA events and node provisioning?

ops-bot: HPA event stream:
```
2026-03-17T17:03:05Z HPA: desired=12 current=6 lastScaleTime=2026-03-17T17:03:05Z
2026-03-17T17:04:40Z HPA: desired=18 current=12 lastScaleTime=2026-03-17T17:04:40Z
2026-03-17T17:06:10Z HPA: desired=24 current=18 lastScaleTime=2026-03-17T17:06:10Z
```

jun: kube nodes are provisioning but GPU images take long to warm up. Warmup logs show repeated slow container init times (~90-120s).

maya: key hypothesis: autoscaler increased replicas but GPU pods are cold and warmup (model weight load/quantization init) causes them to not accept traffic fast enough -> queue backpressure and P99 latency. Also GPU pool near saturation so provisioning queued.

li: logs from runtime (snippet):
```
[2026-03-17T17:05:12Z] pool-manager: allocation_request queue_pos=832
[2026-03-17T17:05:55Z] runtime: model_load_start model=rw-instruct-13b quant=8bit
[2026-03-17T17:07:27Z] runtime: model_ready id=pod-xx-7f
[2026-03-17T17:07:31Z] runtime: accept_connection client=req-19923
```

maya: queue depth at peak 1.4k, avg warmup ~2m. That matches the gap between HPA desired and actual ready pods.

claire: checking GPU pool logs: cloud provider throttled new GPU allocations due to soft quota; there are 3 pending allocation requests. That explains delay in increasing capacity.

maya: mitigation path: 1) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant (rw-instruct-6b) for non-SLO-critical customers; 2) temporarily increase per-customer concurrency cap to shed heavy single-customer traffic? actually lower concurrency cap for that partner to reduce head-of-line blocking; 3) manually bump reserved instance count or request burst capacity from infra.

sam: sending partner a heads-up DM and throttling their traffic by 4x from edge (we have rate limit override).

maya: actioned: applied rate limit rule for partner at 17:16 UTC -> their QPS dropped ~65%. Also enabled routing rule to send non-premium requests to rw-instruct-6b at 17:18 UTC.

ops-bot: routing change applied: route-id=route-evict-1732 -> dest=rw-instruct-6b, sample=100% for partner X.

jun: after routing change, queue_depth reduced to ~400 within 6 minutes, P95 improved. But P99 still elevated due to remaining warmup backlog.

li: manual request to cloud for quota bump submitted at 17:22; provider acknowledged and started allocation, new GPUs arriving ~17:32.

maya: note down in-thread timeline for RCA:
- 17:02 partner traffic surge begins
- 17:03 HPA scales desired up from 6 -> 12
- 17:04 queue depth crosses 1200 threshold, alert fires
- 17:05 autoscaler further desired -> 18, but nodes not yet ready
- 17:07 first new pods become ready but still significantly behind queue consumption
- 17:16 applied partner rate limit; 17:18 routing to 6b enabled
- 17:32 cloud quota allocation starts delivering GPUs; warmup continues until ~17:40
- 17:45 system back to normal baseline

sam: hypothesis tracking: primary root cause = capacity shortfall combined with long warmup time for pods + cloud quota throttle. Secondary = lack of pre-warmed standby for peak partner traffic pattern. Tertiary = routing policies allowed heavy partner to occupy most of the queue (head-of-line).

maya: logs attached (pasted below) and a short trace for a slow request:
```
req-17822 timeline:
17:03:22 queued pos=998
17:04:50 assigned to pod pod-yy-3f
17:07:29 pod-yy-3f finished model_load at 17:07:27
17:07:32 token_stream_start
17:08:10 client-timeout
```

jun: suggestion for live mitigation playbook items (to turn into runbook updates):
- pre-warm buffer: keep N standby pods in each pool for model variants that are heavy and used by large partners
- HPA tuning: add a headroom factor to desired replicas to account for warmup lag (e.g., desired += ceil(inflight / avg_warmup_rate))
- graceful degradation: auto-route to smaller model variant when queue depth threshold hit
- quota monitoring: add alert for cloud allocation throttles / pending GPU requests

li: agreed. Also recommend we add a short-circuit: if gpu_pool_util > 90% and pending_allocations > 2 -> trigger burst request to partner with API to throttle or route.

maya: next steps:
- create RCA doc and assign owners (maya: timeline + mitigation, jun: runbook changes, li: cloud quota monitoring metric, sam: customer comms + post-incident partner follow-up).
- follow-up incident review tomorrow at 10:00 UTC.

claire: I'll capture the cloud side evidence and attach support ticket id #CS-48921.

maya: thanks everyone. leaving a brief postmortem outline in #postmortems after this thread. If anything else shows up, ping me. :white_check_mark:
